newsitem.title: USA: China dissident, journalists win U.S. awards.
newsitem.headline: China dissident, journalists win U.S. awards.

text.p: A Chinese-American group on Monday named a leading Chinese dissident, a Hong Kong journalist and a former New York Times editor as winners of its annual awards for advancing democracy in China.

The Chinese Democracy Education Foundation, a San Francisco-based group that aims to promote democracy and human rights in China, said it was giving one of its "distinguished persons for the advancement of democracy in China" awards to dissident Chen Ziming.
Chen, 42, was sentenced to a 13-year prison term in China in 1991 for engaging in subversive activities during the 1989 pro-democracy protests centered on Beijing's Tiananmen Square.

He was released on bail for medical treatment in 1994 but sent back to prison a year later. He was released again in November last year for medical treatment. Chen has been treated for cancer and hepatitis and suffers from a number of other ailments.
"We are very concerned about human rights conditions in China," David Ai, one of the foundation's directors, said. "We have seen the human rights situation worsen dramatically over this last year."

He said the Clinton administration's China policy had been bankrupt so far, but the foundation hoped the appointment of Madeleine Albright as the new secretary of state would produce "something more tangible."
Also chosen for awards were Hu Chu-Jen, who has worked as a journalist and editor at several Hong Kong publications, and A.M. Rosenthal, a columnist and former executive editor of The New York Times.
Since Chinese authorities used arms and tanks to suppress 1989 pro-democracy protests, Rosenthal had "unceasingly written commentaries advocating human rights in China," the foundation said.
A panel of 19 judges, mostly academics, nominated the award winners, who also receive a prize of $2,000. The award is in its 11th year.
In 1993, the foundation selected Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten for an award for promoting democracy in China, but Patten refused to accept it.
